feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear progression, relevant leadership scope, and solid alignment to digital communications/strategy roles. Writing is polished and professional overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong domain credibility: Drupal, analytics stack, multimedia, governance, and advocacy/public-sector communications are all well evidenced.  
- Good clarity and readability in the profile and experience sections; achievements like the 10,000+ page migration and in-house studio build stand out.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope/activity: e.g., email growth, engagement lifts, conversion improvements, cost savings, team size, budget size, or efficiency gains.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “content operations and enterprise web improvement” reads awkwardly—consider “content operations, and enterprise web improvements” or “enterprise web optimization.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the experience section, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with seniority and scope: emphasize digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter, more executive framing.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial workflows, analytics, and digital systems that improve coordination at scale. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is useful, but avoid adding more platform/tool detail here since later sections cover it well.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper phrasing and pluralize where needed: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial workflow & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow automation & systems design • Stakeholder coordination & cross-functional collaboration • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider replacing “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Workflow automation & systems design” to sound clearer and less inflated.
- Align style with the rest of the CV: “communications” is more consistent than “communication.”
- If space is tight, prioritize the most current differentiators: digital strategy, CMS/platforms, analytics, governance, and AI/search-related systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level while Topline Skills carries the detail.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and the Recent Projects section. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant-level scope, recent strategic impact, and only the work not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line rather than listing each separately.
- Add outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, faster publishing workflows, reduced support issues, or engagement improvements.
- Rephrase technical execution to show business value: “Built Drupal microsites and modular campaign components that improved launch speed and content reuse” rather than “Deliver CMS development…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects entry; keep one concise mention here and let the project section carry detail.
- Governance, analytics, and Drupal platform work also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; focus this item on post-employment consulting scope and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/enterprise scope, and the biggest differentiators versus the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine channel oversight into one impact-focused bullet and add outcomes where possible: email engagement growth, social growth, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make the studio/analytics bullets more results-driven: note increased in-house production capacity, reduced vendor reliance, faster reporting, or better executive decision-making.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at the strategic/enterprise level, not day-to-day execution.
- Video program language may duplicate older NACo entries and Recent Projects; focus here on building the in-house studio and scaling capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel growth, and systems/process improvements rather than broad ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”  
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership where accurate: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is very close to the Director role’s channel-overview language.
- “Weekly video updates” repeats the 2015–2018 entry; frame this role as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector work more distinctly.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to current scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Keep wording parallel and specific; avoid vague labels like “leadership” without context.
- If space allows, prioritize “content operations” and “campaign storytelling” over generic “communications.”
- Consider aligning terminology with recent experience: “enterprise web improvement,” “governance,” and “AI-enabled discovery” are stronger differentiators.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles; tighten or swap for a more distinctive capability.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with highest-value, recent strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation, API integrations.
- Remove lower-priority or older items here if they’re already detailed elsewhere; keep this as a positioning summary, not a full inventory.
- Tighten phrasing and group related skills for readability, e.g.:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- Airtable-based content and operational systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- If possible, align wording to proven outcomes from recent roles, e.g. “enterprise CMS modernization” rather than just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid listing every platform/tool in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and project content; keep wording consistent but not repetitive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and business impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets.
- Replace weaker phrases like “Leadership reporting” with stronger, outcome-oriented language such as “executive dashboarding” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and KPI framework design - Executive dashboarding and decision-ready reporting - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity - SEO, user behavior and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- Since recent NACo roles already mention the analytics stack, avoid repeating every tool here unless framed at a higher strategic level.

- Rewrite as tighter, higher-signal phrases: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and slightly redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add level/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migration, custom content structures) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put **Drupal first** and add brief context to reflect your most recent, highest-impact work without turning this into a sentence.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just “Power Pages.”
- If space allows elsewhere, consider adding proficiency cues only for strongest tools, e.g., **Drupal (advanced)**, rather than labeling every platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one platform-only and the other modernization/implementation-focused.
- GitHub Pages is the least supported by the experience section; cut it first if you need space.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group them more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Separate tooling from coding for clarity: “Technical tooling: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or use context from recent work: e.g., “for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight edge/serverless tasks”
- Consider dropping versioned labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you want this section strictly implementation-focused

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split into two tighter groups to show intent, not just tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and “Work management/collaboration: Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.”
- Cut lower-value or redundant tools unless they were materially used recently; Basecamp and Trello feel older/less strategic given your recent enterprise leadership scope.
- If space allows, rename the heading to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” for clarity.
- Best version: add light proficiency/context, e.g. “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier (workflow automation); Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams (project coordination).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them verbatim in both places.
- Collaboration tools like Slack/Teams are common and may not add much unless paired with stronger systems tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it’s currently just a vendor list. Make it sharper by signaling enterprise email/marketing automation capability and aligning terminology with the experience section.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/level elsewhere or in a short qualifier: **enterprise email operations, newsletter distribution, marketing automation**
- Keep product names current and standardized; “Customer Insights / Journeys” reads less polished than the official product naming.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated email/channel references in multiple NACo roles; avoid restating newsletter scale here unless you remove it from older roles.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused rather than descriptive.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale or outputs you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add specific outputs/scale where possible: website refresh scope, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, email volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and supervised a digital media associate’s day-to-day work.”
- If accurate, split into 2 bullets for readability: one on team/workflow buildout, one on website/content production impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or piloting the format.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; frame this as initial process-building rather than broader operational leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: audience reached, number of episodes, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider a stronger action/result version: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, creating a new multimedia channel for member education and policy storytelling.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later digital roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia work here; save space for the podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
